text_blocks.snippet: Lyme disease can indeed affect the eyes, leading to various visual disturbances and eye-related issues. These can range from mild symptoms like conjunctivitis (pink eye) to more serious conditions like inflammation of the optic nerve (optic neuritis) or even uveitis.
snippet_highlighted_words: leading to various visual disturbances and eye-related issues

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at how Lyme disease impacts the eyes:

list.title: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye):
list.snippet: This is a common early symptom, causing redness, itching, and discharge in the eyes.

list.title: Inflammation:
list.snippet: Lyme disease can cause inflammation of various eye tissues, including the conjunctiva, cornea (keratitis), and the middle layer of the eye (uveitis).

list.title: Optic Nerve Inflammation (Optic Neuritis):
list.snippet: This can lead to vision loss, pain during eye movement, and changes in color perception.

list.title: Other Visual Disturbances:
list.snippet: Patients may experience double vision, blurred vision, floaters, light sensitivity, and difficulty with visual tasks like reading.

list.title: Cranial Nerve Palsies:
list.snippet: In some cases, Lyme disease can affect the nerves that control eye muscles, leading to double vision or other eye movement problems.

list.title: Brain-Related Visual Issues:
list.snippet: Lyme disease can also affect how the brain processes visual information, leading to difficulties with spatial-visual processing, which can manifest as eyestrain, headaches, and problems in crowded environments.
Eye symptoms can occur at different stages of Lyme disease, from early to late.
If you suspect Lyme disease, it's crucial to seek prompt medical attention for diagnosis and treatment.
Early treatment with antibiotics is essential to prevent complications, including those affecting the eyes.
Visual rehabilitation may be necessary in some cases to address visual processing issues.
A neuro-optometrist can provide specialized care for vision problems related to Lyme disease.
